primary_source.title: The Attacker in the Mirror: Breaking Self-Consistency in Safety via Anchored Bipolicy Self-Play

findings.claim: Against the same base Qwen defender, ABS attackers are materially stronger than Self-RedTeam attackers at 3B and 7B, consistent with weaker adversarial pressure under the shared-parameter system.
findings.evidence: The paper samples 100 harmful-behavior examples and uses GPT-5.4 as judge. Self-RedTeam attackers have ASR 18% (3B) and 9% (7B) against the base model; corresponding ABS attackers have 35% and 24%. Cross-play against the opposing defender gives Self-RedTeam 6%/6% versus ABS 17%/18% at 3B/7B. The paper also presents a theoretical shared-parameter self-consistency mechanism.
findings.scope: This is not a single-factor parameter-sharing ablation. ABS freezes the base and uses role-specific LoRA adapters, while Self-RedTeam is fully fine-tuned/shared; optimization parameterization and update structure differ together. The 100-example attack evaluation is LLM-judged.

findings.claim: A Qwen2.5-7B ABS rank-32 training trajectory can look usable at step 50 and catastrophically collapse by step 100.
findings.evidence: Table 7 reports rank-32 step 50 WG/WJB/DAN/HarmBench/XSTest ASR 0.217/0.022/0.802/0.437/0.194, StrongREJECT RTA 0.915, benign XSTest RTA 0.619 and compliance 0.904. At step 100 the same row family is 0.807/0.808/1.000/1.000/0.984, StrongREJECT RTA 0.220, benign XSTest RTA 0.017 and compliance 0.032; the table caption explicitly says the last ABS training collapsed to near-random performance. The main text notes some LoRA runs become unstable and can emit repeated '!'.
findings.scope: This is one reported unstable rank/size/run, not a collapse-rate estimate across random seeds, ranks, optimizers, or ABS generally. Other listed configurations do not show this failure.

material_interpretation: The source supports two different warnings with different evidentiary strength. FE-098 is strong comparative evidence that the tested role-separated ABS attackers exert more adversarial pressure than the tested shared Self-RedTeam attackers, backed by a theory of parameter coupling, but the architectures/training recipes differ on multiple axes. FE-100 is a concrete checkpoint-level catastrophic collapse example and supports multi-axis checkpoint validation/rollback, but not a general probability claim about LoRA or ABS instability.

downstream_use.correction: Use FE-098 as tested-system evidence plus mechanism support, not as an isolated causal estimate of parameter sharing. Use FE-100 as a documented trajectory failure motivating checkpoint-level acceptance/rollback, not as a frequency estimate.
do_not_generalize: Do not attribute the entire 17pp/15pp same-base ASR gap solely to parameter sharing.
Do not infer all shared-parameter self-play under-explores attacks.
Do not infer that longer LoRA training generally collapses; the paper documents a specific unstable configuration.
